entries.ex: The graph shows that the number of online shoppers *increased* every year from 2015 to 2020.
entries.exAr: يوضح الرسم البياني أن عدد المتسوقين عبر الإنترنت *ازداد* كل عام من 2015 إلى 2020.

entries.ex: There was a steep *decline* in printed newspaper sales after 2008.
entries.exAr: شهدت مبيعات الصحف الورقية *تراجعا* حادا بعد عام 2008.

entries.ex: Oil prices *fluctuated* wildly over the period shown, ranging from $40 to $110 a barrel.
entries.exAr: *تذبذبت* أسعار النفط بشدة خلال الفترة المعروضة، إذ تراوحت بين 40 و110 دولارات للبرميل.

entries.ex: Electricity use *peaks* in the early evening, when most people return home.
entries.exAr: يبلغ استهلاك الكهرباء *ذروته* في أول المساء، حين يعود معظم الناس إلى منازلهم.

entries.ex: After rising quickly for five years, unemployment *levelled off* at around 6%.
entries.exAr: بعد ارتفاع سريع دام خمس سنوات، *استقرت* نسبة البطالة عند نحو 6%.

entries.ex: The birth rate *remained stable* at 1.8 children per woman throughout the period.
entries.exAr: ظل معدل المواليد *مستقرا* عند 1.8 طفل لكل امرأة طوال الفترة.

entries.ex: House prices in the capital *soared* by 40% in just three years.
entries.exAr: *قفزت* أسعار المنازل في العاصمة بنسبة 40% في ثلاث سنوات فقط.

entries.ex: Visitor numbers *plummeted* from 2 million to just 300,000 when the borders closed.
entries.exAr: *هوت* أعداد الزوار من مليوني زائر إلى 300 ألف فقط عندما أغلقت الحدود.

entries.ex: The chart shows a *gradual* rise in the average age of first-time mothers.
entries.exAr: يبين المخطط ارتفاعا *تدريجيا* في متوسط عمر الأمهات عند الولادة الأولى.

entries.ex: Recycling rates showed *steady* growth, rising by about two percentage points a year.
entries.exAr: أظهرت معدلات إعادة التدوير نموا *مطردا*، إذ ارتفعت بنحو نقطتين مئويتين سنويا.

entries.ex: The data reveal a *sharp* drop in car sales during the first quarter of the year.
entries.exAr: تكشف البيانات عن انخفاض *حاد* في مبيعات السيارات خلال الربع الأول من العام.

entries.ex: Smartphone ownership saw a *dramatic* increase, from 20% to 85% of adults in a decade.
entries.exAr: شهدت نسبة امتلاك الهواتف الذكية زيادة *هائلة*، من 20% إلى 85% من البالغين خلال عقد.

entries.ex: June saw a *slight* decrease in rainfall, from 42 mm to 39 mm.
entries.exAr: شهد شهر يونيو انخفاضا *طفيفا* في كمية الأمطار، من 42 ملم إلى 39 ملم.

entries.ex: A *significant* number of respondents said they had never used public transport.
entries.exAr: قال عدد *كبير* من المشاركين في الاستطلاع إنهم لم يستخدموا وسائل النقل العام قط.

entries.ex: The *proportion* of women in senior management rose from 15% to 28%.
entries.exAr: ارتفعت *نسبة* النساء في المناصب الإدارية العليا من 15% إلى 28%.

entries.ex: The *percentage* of households with internet access reached 95% in 2020.
entries.exAr: بلغت *النسبة المئوية* للأسر التي لديها اتصال بالإنترنت 95% عام 2020.

entries.ex: The vast *majority* of students surveyed preferred studying in the morning.
entries.exAr: فضلت *الغالبية* العظمى من الطلاب المشمولين بالاستطلاع الدراسة صباحا.

entries.ex: Renewable energy produced only a *fraction* of the country's electricity in 2005.
entries.exAr: لم تنتج الطاقة المتجددة سوى *جزء ضئيل* من كهرباء البلاد عام 2005.

entries.ex: *Approximately* one in five adults in the survey worked from home.
entries.exAr: كان *نحو* واحد من كل خمسة بالغين في الاستطلاع يعمل من المنزل.

entries.ex: Coffee and tea accounted for 45% and 30% of hot drink sales, *respectively*.
entries.exAr: استحوذت القهوة والشاي على 45% و30% من مبيعات المشروبات الساخنة *على التوالي*.

entries.ex: In 2010 the *figure* for Spain was just 12%, compared with 30% for Italy.
entries.exAr: في عام 2010 بلغ *الرقم* الخاص بإسبانيا 12% فقط، مقارنة بنسبة 30% لإيطاليا.

entries.ex: The statistics point to a clear *trend* towards smaller families in urban areas.
entries.exAr: تشير الإحصاءات إلى *اتجاه* واضح نحو الأسر الأصغر حجما في المناطق الحضرية.

entries.ex: *Overall*, spending on healthcare rose in all five countries over the period.
entries.exAr: *إجمالا*، ارتفع الإنفاق على الرعاية الصحية في البلدان الخمسة جميعها خلال الفترة.

entries.ex: Tourism *accounts for* nearly a quarter of the island's income.
entries.exAr: *تشكل* السياحة ما يقارب ربع دخل الجزيرة.

entries.ex: The number of electric cars on the world's roads more than *doubled* between 2019 and 2021.
entries.exAr: زاد عدد السيارات الكهربائية على طرق العالم إلى *أكثر من الضعف* بين عامي 2019 و2021.

entries.ex: On *average*, teenagers in the survey spent four hours a day online.
entries.exAr: في *المتوسط*، قضى المراهقون المشمولون بالاستطلاع أربع ساعات يوميا على الإنترنت.

entries.ex: Experts *estimate* that about a third of all food produced worldwide is wasted.
entries.exAr: *يقدّر* الخبراء أن نحو ثلث الغذاء المنتج في العالم يهدر.

entries.ex: According to *projections*, the proportion of people over 65 in the country will reach 25% by 2050.
entries.exAr: تشير *التوقعات* إلى أن نسبة من تزيد أعمارهم على 65 عاما في البلاد ستبلغ 25% بحلول عام 2050.

entries.ex: Fees at private universities were *considerably* higher than at public ones.
entries.exAr: كانت الرسوم في الجامعات الخاصة أعلى *بكثير* منها في الجامعات الحكومية.

entries.ex: Bus use fell only *marginally*, from 31% of journeys to 30%.
entries.exAr: انخفض استخدام الحافلات انخفاضا *طفيفا* فقط، من 31% من الرحلات إلى 30%.

gap.s: Wheat prices ____ throughout the year, rising and falling almost every month.
Sales ____ from 500,000 to just 50,000 units after the product was withdrawn.
After a period of rapid growth, subscriber numbers began to ____ at around 2 million.
In 2020, private cars ____ almost 70% of all journeys to work.
France and Germany recorded growth of 2% and 3% ____.
The ____ of adults who smoke has fallen from one in four to one in eight.
Thanks to new machinery, the factory managed to ____ its output in just two years.
Visitor numbers usually ____ in August, when schools are on holiday.

para.a: Prices went up very quickly and by a huge amount in 2022.
para.b: Prices *soared* in 2022, reaching a record high.

para.a: Most of the people in the survey said they liked the new park.
para.b: The *majority* of respondents expressed approval of the new park.

para.a: About half of the money was spent on rent.
para.b: Rent *accounted for* approximately half of total spending.

para.a: The number of tourists went down a little in 2019.
para.b: There was a *slight* decline in tourist numbers in 2019.

p1.q: Do you like working with numbers?
p1.a: To be honest, I quite enjoy it. In my job I often have to read sales *figures* and spot a *trend*, and I find it satisfying when the numbers tell a clear story. Complicated statistics can be tiring, though.

p1.q: How often do you look at charts or graphs?
p1.a: Almost every day, actually. The news is full of them, and my banking app shows a chart of my monthly spending. It's quite useful, because I can see at a glance when my expenses *increase* or when I'm saving more.

p1.q: Has the way you use your phone changed in recent years?
p1.a: Definitely. My screen time has nearly *doubled* since I started university, mainly because I now use my phone for studying and paying for things. I'm trying to cut down, but it isn't easy.

p2.cue: Describe a change in your town or city that you have noticed.
points: and explain how you feel about this change
p2.a: I'd like to describe the *dramatic* growth in the number of cafés in my home town. When I was a child, there were only two or three, but around eight years ago new ones started opening almost every month. I'd *estimate* that there are now *approximately* forty in the town centre alone, and the number has more than *doubled* in the last five years. The change has affected people in several ways. On the positive side, cafés have created jobs, especially for young people, and they give students a comfortable place to meet and study. On the other hand, rents on the main street have *soared*, and a *significant* number of small family shops have closed because they simply couldn't compete. So I have mixed feelings about it. I enjoy having so many places to relax with friends, but I worry that the town is slowly losing its character. I'd like to see a better balance between new businesses and traditional shops.

p3.q: Why do you think people are often misled by statistics?
p3.a: Mainly because numbers look objective, so people rarely question them. A headline might say that burglaries in a small village have *increased* by 50%, which sounds alarming, but if the original *figure* was just two cases, the rise is actually tiny. Many people also confuse an *average* with what is typical. That's why I think schools should teach basic data skills.

p3.q: How might governments use data to plan for the future?
p3.a: Data is extremely valuable for long-term planning. For instance, population *projections* allow governments to calculate how many schools or hospitals will be needed in twenty years' time. Similarly, if traffic data shows a clear *trend* towards more cars in a particular area, planners can invest in public transport before congestion becomes serious. The key, of course, is that the data must be accurate and regularly updated.

writing.q: The graph below shows the percentage of journeys to work that were made by car, bus and bicycle in a European city between 2000 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay: The line graph illustrates the *proportion* of journeys to work that were made by car, bus and bicycle in a European city over a twenty-year period from 2000 to 2020.

*Overall*, the car remained the most common way of commuting throughout the period, although its share fell after 2005. Cycling, by contrast, showed the most striking growth, and by 2020 it had overtaken the bus.

In 2000, cars *accounted for* 62% of journeys, and this figure rose to a *peak* of 66% five years later. It then dipped *marginally* to 64% in 2010 before a *sharp* fall to 55% in 2015 and 48% in 2020. Bus use, meanwhile, dropped from 25% to 22% between 2000 and 2005 and then *remained stable* at 22–23% for the rest of the period.

Cycling followed a very different pattern. Only 5% of commuters travelled by bicycle in 2000, and the rise was *gradual* at first, to 6% in 2005 and 9% in 2010. After this, however, the figure *soared*, climbing to 16% in 2015 and 24% in 2020, almost five times its original level. As a result, bicycles were used for 24% of journeys in the final year, compared with 22% for buses.
